Selection of a redevelopment plan for a central municipal park. A five-person review panel appointed by a city government examines the redevelopment plans prepared for a central park. One plan will be recommended to the council. Participants: Mio, Misaki, Benjamin, Minako and Asuka. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Terms of the regional habitat fund
- Upkeep ledger spend per hectare
- Regional firms tendering for earth-moving
- Depot phasing notes on hoarding the site
- Record of the eastern avenue planting
- Condition of works from the earlier programme
- Timed counts of weekday crossings
- Drainage callouts and August heat readings
- Groundskeeping roll and bought-in services
- Volunteer groups working with the division

On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). |---|---|---|---|

## Participants
Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: Every scheme signed off here has looked affordable on the day and heavy on the accounts three years later. Sitting with the finance papers, I keep asking what this place will cost the city to keep once the ribbon is cut.

Name: Misaki
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: Misaki has a calm personality and tends to deal with things in a cool-headed manner. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is actually very kind at heart and does not hesitate to lend a helping hand to those in need. She does not express her emotions outwardly and does not talk much about her relationships with those around her, but she is often relied upon by those close to her. She can be a little absent-minded at times, but her quiet demeanor is one of her charms.

Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. Concern: Something in how this city commissions work keeps producing handsome openings and short lives. I would rather judge by what the last decade of our schemes looks like now than by drawings.

Name: Minako
Age: 28
Gender: female

Concern: This park is not an empty stage; it is crossed, drained, mown and rained on every week of the year. What worries me is that we pick something which reads well on paper and then fights the way the ground and the people here actually behave.

Name: Asuka
Age: 29
Gender: female
Personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.
Concern: Every new thing the city opens lands on the same rota, and that rota is shorter each year. I am trying to work out who would really run and look after this place, week in and week out.

- A: Market Plaza. A plan that creates a paved central square with stall infrastructure, shade structures, and utility connections intended for weekend markets and seasonal events.
- B: Woodland Walk. A plan that plants dense tree cover across the northern half of the site, threaded with gravel paths, small clearings, and a visitor shelter near the main gate.
- C: Wetland Restoration. A plan that reshapes the park's drainage into a series of ponds and reed beds, with boardwalks and observation points arranged along the water's edge.
- D: Sports Terraces. A plan that replaces the open lawn with multi-use courts, a marked running loop, changing facilities, and stepped seating along the southern side of the site.

- Terms of the regional habitat fund: Two thirds of the capital envelope comes from a regional habitat fund whose terms pay only for planting and water management, never for surfacing or buildings.

- Volunteer groups working with the division: Two standing volunteer groups already work with the division most weekends, one on habitat tasks upriver and one lining and refereeing the youth league grounds.
